candidates.change_summary: Change support check so it does NOT include IERC1155MetadataURI interface id (removes that branch), causing different return for that interface id.
Invert check for IERC1155 so supportsInterface returns true only for IERC1155MetadataURI and not for IERC1155 itself.
Require that both IERC1155 and IERC1155MetadataURI match (AND) instead of either (OR), so only an id matching both returns true, changing observed results.
Always defer to super.supportsInterface (remove explicit checks), causing interface ids formerly recognized here to possibly return different values.
Change the balanceOf check to allow zero-address and return 0 instead of reverting for address(0).
Remove the require and always return stored balance (which will be 0 for zero address) without any check.
Invert the zero-address check to revert when account is non-zero (so non-zero accounts revert), returning balance only for zero address.
Removed the require check that forbids querying balanceOf for the zero address so calling balanceOf(address(0), id) now returns 0 instead of reverting.
Change the equality-length check requirement to allow callers to supply longer ids than accounts by truncating to the accounts length instead of reverting.
Compute each batch balance using the id at position 0 for all accounts instead of the corresponding id, making results depend only on accounts and the first id.
Change the loop to iterate using a signed int starting at -1 and pre-increment, causing it to skip the first account and shift all indices by one.

Change loop to iterate using a strict < accounts.length instead of <=, causing omission of last element if lengths mismatched externally (introduces different returned balances when called with valid equal-length arrays by skipping final account).
Return zeroed balances immediately when accounts array is empty rather than returning an empty array (changes observable output for empty inputs).
Use unchecked increment in loop to alter overflow behavior (though safe here, it still changes bytecode and could affect edge-case behaviour with extremely large length values).
Call balanceOf with reversed arguments (ids[i], accounts[i]) causing incorrect indexing and thus different returned balances.
